jobs.title: Holocaust Education Facilitator at Sandra Bornstein Holocaust Education Center
jobs.description: Employer: Sandra Bornstein Holocaust Education Center Expires: 10/01/2026 Holocaust Education Program FacilitatorSandra Bornstein Holocaust Education Center | Providence, RIThe Sandra Bornstein Holocaust Education Center is seeking an engaging Facilitator for READ, our new after-school Holocaust education program for students in grades 6–8, two to three hours/week, Wednesday afternoons, 3-5 PM. READ brings history to life through books, comics, art, photographs, primary sources, survivor testimony, and hands-on projects. The facilitator will work with Center staff to lead activities and discussions, support students, and create an engaging and welcoming learning environment.Responsibilities:Help lead weekly discussions, readings, art activities, and hands-on projectsEngage students with historical sources, literature, and survivor testimonySupport classroom management and an inclusive learning environmentAssist with program materials and student projectsWe’re looking for someone who:Enjoys working with middle school studentsHas experience in education, youth programming, museums, history, Holocaust studies, or a related fieldIs dependable, organized, collaborative, and comfortable discussing challenging history with young peopleKnowledge of the Holocaust required. Training, curriculum, lesson plans, and materials are provided.Schedule: Wednesdays, 3:00–4:00 p.m., September 30–December 16, 2026, excluding school holidays, plus paid preparation timeLocation: Sandra Bornstein Holocaust Education Center, 401 Elmgrove Ave., ProvidenceCompensation: $35/hour.To apply, send a résumé and brief statement of interest to info@hercri.org, including a little about your experience working with young people and your interest in the program.

jobs.title: Instructor (PAC) Pool - Spring, Summer, and Fall 2026: Aerobics & Fitness Development (Rhythmic Cardio Formats) at Oregon State University
jobs.description: Employer: Oregon State University Expires: 10/01/2026 Instructor (PAC) Pool - Spring, Summer, and Fall 2026: Aerobics & Fitness Development (Rhythmic Cardio Formats)Oregon State UniversityDepartment: Physical ActivityCourses (HHS)Appointment Type: Academic FacultyJob Location: CorvallisRecommended Full-Time Salary Range: Salary is commensurate with skills, education, and experience.Job Summary:The Physical Activities Course (PAC) program, a part of the School of Exercise, Sport, and Health Sciences, in the College of Health at Oregon State University invites applications for one or more fixed-term, non-tenure track full/part-time Aerobics & Fitness Development (Rhythmic Cardio Formats) Instructor (PAC) positions to teach courses on a term-by-term basis for the Spring, Summer, and Fall terms in the 2026 academic year.Some of these appointments may be reviewed for renewal or transition to an instructional position on an annual basis at the discretion of the program Director. Applications submitted to this recruitment pool are reviewed on an as needed basis. Qualified candidates will be contacted when positions become available. Scheduling for each term is determined in February for Spring term, November for Winter term, and beginning in May for Fall term.The primary mission of the PAC Program is to provide all Oregon State University students with the knowledge and experience to make sound decisions regarding present and future physically active lifestyles. The intent of the PAC Program is to provide quality instruction in safe, adequately equipped facilities and to create a positive, enjoyable learning environment.The PAC Instructor position will serve as an integral member of the PAC program team, where each instructor plays a specific role to the larger organization. Recognizing individual interests and abilities, the program provides courses covering a wide variety of physical activities. We make an effort to address contemporary trends and student interests. Courses offered through the PAC Program may include but are not limited to classes in the areas of: aquatics, artistic & social dance, fitness development, martial arts, mind/body, outdoor recreation, resistance training, sports, and games.For additional information about the PAC program, please visit https://health.oregonstate.edu/pac. Why OSU?Working for Oregon State University is so much more than a job!Oregon State University is a dynamic community of dreamers, doers, problem-solvers and change-makers. We don't wait for challenges to present themselves - we seek them out and take them on. We welcome students, faculty and staff from every background and perspective into a community where everyone feels seen and heard. We have deep-rooted mindfulness for the natural world and all who depend on it, and together, we apply knowledge, tools and skills to build a better future for all.FACTS:• Top 1.4% university in the world• More research funding than all public universities in Oregon combined• 1 of 3 land, sea, space and sun grant universities in the U.S.• 2 campuses, 11 colleges, 12 experiment stations, and Extension programs in all 36 counties• 7 https://hr.oregonstate.edu/work-life/diversity-and-cultural-resources that offer education, celebration and belonging for everyone• 100+ undergraduate degree programs, 80+ graduate degrees plus hundreds of minor options and certificates• 35k+ students including more than 2.3k international students and 10k students of color• 217k+ alumni worldwide• For more interesting facts about OSU visit: https://oregonstate.edu/aboutLocations:Oregon State has a statewide presence with campuses in Corvallis and Bend, the OSU Portland Center and the Hatfield Marine Science Center on the Pacific Coast in Newport.Oregon State's beautiful, historic and state-of-the-art main campus is located in one of America's best college towns. Corvallis is located close to the Pacific Ocean, the Cascade mountains and Oregon wine country. Nestled in the heart of the Willamette Valley, this beautiful city offers miles of mountain biking and hiking trails, a river perfect for boating or kayaking and an eclectic downtown featuring local cuisine, popular events and performances.Total Rewards Package:Oregon State University offers a https://hr.oregonstate.edu/benefits/prospective-employee with benefits eligible positions that is designed to meet the needs of employees and their families including:• Medical, Dental, Vision and Basic Life. OSU pays 95% of premiums for you and your eligible dependents.• Free confidential mental health and emotional support services, and counseling resources.• Retirement savings paid by the university.• A generous paid leave package, including holidays, vacation and sick leave.• Tuition reduction benefits for you or your qualifying dependents at OSU or the additional six Oregon Public Universities.• Robust Work Life programs including Dual Career assistance resources, flexible work arrangements, a Family Resource Center, Affinity Groups and an Employee Assistance Program.• Optional lifestyle benefits such as pet, accident, and critical illness insurance, giving you peace of mind and the support you need to thrive in all aspects of your life.Oregon State University is deeply committed to the principles of a Health Promoting University. This commitment drives a collaborative approach across OSU's safety and well-being programs, reducing silos and coordinating efforts to enhance employee safety and well-being. By prioritizing resources that support the health of both employees and students, OSU fosters a culture of care and a healthier campus environment where everyone can thrive.https://bestplace4workingparents.com/policies/Future and current OSU employees can use the https://hr.oregonstate.edu/benefits/new-employees/benefits-calculator to learn more about the full value of the benefits provided at OSU.Key Responsibilities95% Teaching:Teach courses in Aerobics & Fitness Development, specifically in rhythmic cardio formats.Plan and organize instruction in ways that maximize student learning. Employ appropriate teaching and learning strategies to communicate subject matter to students. Modify, where appropriate, instructional methods and strategies to meet diverse student needs. Employ available instructional technology, i.e. the internet, telecourses, interactive technology, when appropriate. Contribute to the selection and development of instructional materials in accordance with course objectives. Develop, update, and post course syllabi and grades in a timely manner. Respond to emergency situations for the purpose of resolving immediate safety concerns and/or directing to appropriate personnel for resolution.Establish meaningful student learning outcomes for courses/programs. Develop learning assessments that clearly measure student progress toward student learning outcomes. Maintain accurate records of student progress. Demonstrate sensitivity to student needs and circumstances.2.5% Support:Be accessible to colleagues and to students for advisement and consultation. Prepare, distribute, and submit syllabi and approved course outlines for all assigned sections in accordance with program and divisional policies. Maintain confidentiality of student information. Substitute for other instructors within field or discipline in case of an absence.Participate in meetings and events required by the program administrators. Respond in a timely fashion to information requests from college, division, and program administrators.2.5% Personal and Professional Growth:Demonstrate a thorough and accurate knowledge of their field or discipline. Connect their subject matter with related fields. Stay current in their subject matter through professional development, involvement in professional organizations, and attending professional meetings, conferences, certifications or workshops. Learn and use appropriate technologies to enhance teaching and the educational experience when appropriate.Maintain familiarity with college and program goals, mission, and long-range plans. Contribute to planning and development processes through appropriate mechanisms and channels. Perform professional responsibilities in accordance with pertinent goals, missions, and plans of the college, division, and programs. What You Will Need* Bachelor's degree in any field.* Extensive participation or involvement in activity area of expertise within Aerobics & Fitness Development or Professional Certification, when applicable.* Current certifications in a rhythmic cardio format such as Cardio Kickboxing, Cardio Dance, or Step Aerobics.* Current, valid Adult CPR and AED Essentials by the start of classes.* Current, valid First Aid certification by the start of classes.* Evident commitment to educational equity.Final candidates for this position must complete a sexual misconduct reference check, per University Policy 05-010. An offer of employment will be contingent upon satisfactory results from the sexual misconduct reference check.What We Would Like You to Have Bachelor's degree in Exercise Science or closely related discipline OR Master's degree in any field.* Demonstrated ability to design, teach and assess courses that support inclusive learning principles and promote equitable teaching practices, to the benefit of all learners.* Current Group Fitness, Personal Training, or Exercise Specialist Certification.* Previous successful teaching experience in a higher education setting.* Previous experience assessing student learning outcomes and curriculum development. Working Conditions / Work ScheduleIn the performance of the duties of the position, incumbents will be required to lead physical activity courses and demonstrate activity-specific movements for a minimum duration of 50-90 minutes per scheduled class.Special Instructions to ApplicantsApplications will be continue to be considered throughout the Spring, Summer, and Fall term of 2026.When applying you will be required to attach the following electronic documents:1) A Curriculum Vitae; and2) A cover letter indicating how your qualifications and experience have prepared you for this position.3) Licenses/Certification (optional): Please upload any license or certificates required to the position.You will also be required to submit the names of at least three professional references, their e-mail addresses and telephone numbers as part of the application process.For additional information please contact:Katelyn Kirkkatelyn.kirk@oregonstate.eduorJessica Cazejessica.caze@oregonstate.eduorNicole Kurthnicole.kurth@oregonstate.eduApplications will be considered throughout the 2025/2026 academic year as opportunities become available.Starting salary within the salary range will be commensurate with education, experience, and training/certification.Starting salary range for the position of Instructor (PAC) is $32,100-$39,233.Finalists will be required to provide proof of their degree at the time of offer.We are an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability, protected veteran, and other protected status.OSU will conduct a review of the National Sex Offender Public website prior to hire.Final candidates for this position must complete a sexual misconduct reference check, per University Policy 05-010. An offer of employment will be contingent upon satisfactory results from the sexual misconduct reference check.To apply, please visit: https://apptrkr.com/9709406 je-538ad1bb11a945288a4d96bf3cd7323c

jobs.description: Employer: Eastern Suffolk BOCES Expires: 10/01/2026 POSITION: Educational Technology Coach – Multiple Positions (FT - 12 month) An Educational Technology Coach models and facilitates the effective integration of educational technology to enhance teaching and learning. The Educational Technology Coach partners with district educators and leaders to design and implement lessons, learning experiences, and instructional practices that effectively integrate technology and align with district goals. The Educational Technology Coach also facilitates regional professional learning workshops, sharing innovative practices, emerging technologies, and effective instructional strategies with educators across the region. Prepares monthly testing data summary report for the Manager of Academic Testing and other personnel as needed. E. Provides administrative assistance to the Manager of Academic Testing1. Serves as information contact for the Academic Testing Center as workload dictates. 2. Orders, organizes, and maintains office supply inventories and testing materials for the Academic Testing Center. 3. Participates in training sessions which advances professional development and services for the Academic Testing Center and college. 4. Provides support and direction to student workers employed by the Academic Testing Center. 5. Performs other duties as assigned. F. Provides direct support for test takers, faculty, and staff1. Troubleshoots a variety of vendor-specific software issues that may arise.EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCEAssociate’s Degree or the willingness to obtain a degree if hired; Bachelor’s Degree preferred. jobs.description: Employer: Monarch Expires: 10/01/2026 Help people build meaningful careers—and make a lasting impact while you do it. Do you enjoy supporting people as they work toward their goals and aspirations?Are you looking for a mission-driven organization that values choice, dignity, and professional growth? Monarch NC is seeking a passionate and motivated Qualified Mental Health Professional (QMHP) to join our Employment Support team in Charlotte, North Carolina. At Monarch, we are committed to providing high-quality, trauma-informed services that support people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, mental health conditions, and substance use disorders in leading self-directed and fulfilling lives. Your work will focus on collaboration, advocacy, and practical support. Key responsibilities include:Supporting individuals in exploring career interests, employment goals, work history, strengths, cultural identity, justice involvement, and other factors related to vocational successDeveloping, maintaining, and updating individualized career profiles using input from the person supported, treatment team members, and—with permission—family members or former employersCoordinating with individuals and their support teams to develop and update individual employment plansBuilding and maintaining strong partnerships with local employers, businesses, and community organizations to expand volunteer and employment opportunitiesIdentifying new community partners and nurturing ongoing professional relationshipsPromoting self-determination and informed choice throughout the employment process What You’ll BringTo qualify, candidates must meet North Carolina Qualified Mental Health Professional (QMHP) requirements under 10A NCAC 27G .0104, including one of the following: Bachelor’s degree (non–Human Services)4 years full-time or 8 years part-time experience working with adults with a mental health diagnosis, intellectual/developmental disability, and/or substance use disorderBachelor’s degree (Human Services)2 years full-time or 4 years part-time experience working with adults with a mental health diagnosis, intellectual/developmental disability, and/or substance use disorderMaster’s degree (Human Services)1 year full-time or 2 years part-time experience working with adults with a mental health diagnosis, intellectual/developmental disability, and/or substance use disorder Experience in employment services, supported employment, or community-based vocational programs is a plus. Why Work at Monarch?We believe that when our professionals are supported, the people we serve benefit even more. Monarch offers a comprehensive and people-first benefits package, including:Employee Care Fund for staff facing unexpected financial hardshipMedical, Dental, and Vision Insurance (full-time employees)Paid Time Off, plus 10 paid company holidaysEligibility for the Public Service Student Loan Forgiveness ProgramEmployee Development Program and ongoing learning opportunitiesRetirement Plan (full-time employees)Employee Referral ProgramEmployee Assistance Program…and much more Join Our MissionAt Monarch, we support people with disabilities in growing toward their potential, pursuing meaningful goals, and making informed choices about where they live, learn, work, play, and worship. If you’re passionate about employment, inclusion, and empowering people to define success on their own terms, we’d love to hear from you. Come grow with us—we look forward to working together.

jobs.title: Early Intervention Provider — Special Instruction (SWD Birth–Grade 2) at Achievable Milestones Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Achievable Milestones Inc. Expires: 10/01/2026 **PLEASE NOTE: Applicants must hold a Masters in Students with Disabilities Birth- grade 2 or Masters of special education birth- grade 2, otherwise applicants will not be considered for this position. About UsAchievable Milestones Inc. is a New York State–approved Early Intervention agency serving infants, toddlers, and families across New York City, Nassau County, and Westchester County. We provide Special Instruction, Applied Behavior Analysis, Speech-Language Therapy, and Service Coordination — delivered in the home and community, grounded in family coaching and natural-environment practice.We are building our provider team right now. That means you get in early, choose your own service area, and work with a Program Director who picks up the phone. We are a small agency by design: families reach a person who knows their child, and providers reach someone who knows their cases.Who We're HiringSpecial Instruction and ABA providers — both roles require the same New York State credential. NYSED certification as a Teacher of Students with Disabilities, Birth–Grade 2, is required. SWD (All Grades) does not qualify for Early Intervention. The Birth–Grade 2 certificate is required by the State and cannot be substituted.If you also have ABA training and experience, tell us — we assign ABA caseloads to providers with that background, under the clinical supervision of a New York State Licensed Behavior Analyst.A note for behavior analysts: in New York, ABA in Early Intervention is delivered under Special Instruction, so the provider-level credential is the SWD Birth–Grade 2 certification. BCBA certification on its own does not qualify a provider for New York Early Intervention. If you hold a NYS Licensed Behavior Analyst (LBA) license, we are hiring separately at the clinical supervisor level — email us and we'll send you that posting instead.What You'll DoDeliver individualized, evidence-based Early Intervention services in children's homes and natural community settingsUse family-centered, embedded-coaching strategies that give parents and caregivers something they can use in everyday routinesDevelop and work toward functional IFSP outcomes; collaborate with the child's team and other providersComplete timely, compliant session notes, service logs, and quarterly progress reportsMaintain parent/caregiver presence during sessions, as required by New York State EI policyWhat We RequireNYSED certification as a Teacher of Students with Disabilities (Birth–Grade 2) — All Grades does not qualifyEligibility as New York State Early Intervention Qualified PersonnelActive individual NPIAbility to complete the registry clearances required by New York State for anyone working with young children (Justice Center Staff Exclusion List and Statewide Central Register), health and immunization documentation, and required NYS EI trainingsReliable transportation for home and community visitsExperience with infants and toddlers (birth–3) preferredBilingual providers are especially needed — Spanish, Russian, Mandarin, Cantonese, Haitian Creole, Bengali, Urdu, ASL and othersProfessional/Malpractice insurance for 1099 employment CompensationThis is a fee-for-service position — you are paid per session delivered, not per hour, the way Early Intervention is authorized and billed.$45–$80 per session. Where you fall in that range depends on session length (30 or 60 minutes), discipline, county, your experience, and whether you're on W-2 or 1099.1099 rates sit at the higher end of the band — on W-2 we carry the employer share of your payroll taxes, unemployment insurance, and workers' compensation, which a 1099 rate has to cover out of your own pocket. Compare the net, not the headline.A higher rate applies if you hold an individual New York State DOH approval letter — and if you don't have one yet, we will walk you through the application.Payroll is issued bi-weekly. Many agencies in this field pay monthly or on a lag. We don't.W-2 or 1099 — your choice. On W-2, paid sick leave accrues from your first hour worked. 1099 providers supply a Certificate of Insurance or CE-200. 1099 Providers must hold a valid DOH Approval letter. Why Join Achievable MilestonesYou choose your service area. Flexible, self-directed schedulingBi-weekly payFast credentialing. Real clinical and administrative support.How to ApplySubmit your résumé through Indeed, or email hr@achievablemilestones.com with your discipline and the county you'd like to work in.Achievable Milestones Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

Qualified candidates will be contacted when positions become available throughout the academic year. Some of these appointments may be reviewed for renewal or transition to an instructional position on an annual basis at the discretion of the program Director. Scheduling for each term is determined in February for Spring term, November for Winter term, and beginning in May for Fall term.The primary mission of the PAC Program is to provide all Oregon State University students with the knowledge and experience to make sound decisions regarding present and future physically active lifestyles. The intent of the PAC Program is to provide quality instruction in safe, adequately equipped facilities and to create a positive, enjoyable learning environment.The PAC Instructor position will serve as an integral member of the PAC Program team, where each instructor plays a specific role to the larger organization. jobs.title: 4-H Program Manager at UNH - Cooperative Extension
jobs.description: Employer: UNH - Cooperative Extension Expires: 10/01/2026 This position is located at Extension’s Merrimack County office in Boscawen, New Hampshire.The 4-H program manager facilitates the growth of the Merrimack County 4-H program and life-skill development of 4-H youth. This is done primarily through the coordination and mobilization of 110 community- or topic-based 4-H volunteers who recruit, train, support, and guide youth and families through community engagement activities to prepare youth for life and community-ready skills. 4-H, the nation’s largest youth development organization, works in local communities to offer youth online and in-person programming through clubs, collaborative community partnerships, afterschool programs, camps, and other educational activities. N.H. 4-H programs are designed around a pathway model centered on national 4-H mission areas of STEM/agriscience, civic engagement, and healthy living. 4-H pathways engage youth in a sequential learning experience, enabling youth to build mastery of skill and knowledge as well as a sense of belonging to their community and world. This position will have frequent night and weekend programmatic responsibilities due to the nature of working with volunteers and youth events outside of the school day. There is flexibility in fixed times for hours worked weekly to accommodate community realities in programming. When determined appropriate with supervisor and Extension administration, this position may serve as the county office administrator (COA) of the Merrimack County Extension office. jobs.title: GGO Capacity Building Associate VISTA at Gateway to the Great Outdoors (GGO)
jobs.description: Employer: Gateway to the Great Outdoors (GGO) Expires: 10/01/2026 Gateway to the Great Outdoors (GGO) provides students living in low-income St.Louis communities with comprehensive STEM education. The mission of GGO is to engage students with the outdoors through experiential learning and mentorship to improve academic engagement and social-emotional skills through classroom and field-based educational experiences. The proposed AmeriCorps VISTA project will support GGO’s expansion of programming into the Ferguson-Florissant school district. The GGO Capacity Building Associate VISTA members will build GGO’s capacity by researching and helping to implement procedures that support GGO’s reach into Ferguson-Florissant District partner schools in Ferguson, Missouri. As a result of VISTA members’ service, approximately 200 students living in low-income communities will have access to an enhanced STEM curriculum to improve student academic engagement with science education and social-emotional skills, and members will establish a sustainable funding plan that supports the long-term impact of GGO programs. GGO education programming and mentorship provide students the skills and resources to direct them on a course to be lifted out of poverty and pursue academic and professional careers in STEM.

jobs.description: Employer: Oregon State University Expires: 10/01/2026 Professional Development for Educators Pool- Spring & Fall 2026 (Counselor, Adult, and Higher Education) Oregon State University Department: College of Education (KED) Appointment Type: Professional Faculty Job Location: Corvallis Recommended Full-Time Salary Range: $28.00 - $31.00 Job Summary: The College of Education's Professional Development for Educators program invites applications for one or more part-time professional faculty positions to develop and/or deliver professional development courses and workshops for Spring and Fall of the 2026 academic year. Applications submitted to this recruitment pool are reviewed on an as needed basis. Qualified candidates will be contacted when positions become available. These positions will develop and/or deliver professional development courses and workshops for the Spring and Fall of the 2026 academic year. The purpose of this position is to develop and/or deliver online training programs for the College of Education's Professional Development for Educators program. These are noncredit courses open to academic, corporate, teaching and training professionals. This position does not formally grade work or provide academic advising but will deliver and facilitate largely peer-to-peer interactions and provide formative feedback to students in various education related disciplines using Canvas/ Catalog LMS platforms. The College of Education strives to be an international leader in research and in the preparation of change agents in education and related fields. The vision of the College is to develop change agents in the form of researchers, scholars, learning leaders, teachers and counselors. Why OSU? Working for Oregon State University is so much more than a job! Oregon State University is a dynamic community of dreamers, doers, problem-solvers and change-makers. We don't wait for challenges to present themselves - we seek them out and take them on. We welcome students, faculty and staff from every background and perspective into a community where everyone feels seen and heard. We have deep-rooted mindfulness for the natural world and all who depend on it, and together, we apply knowledge, tools and skills to build a better future for all. FACTS: • Top 1.4% university in the world • More research funding than all public universities in Oregon combined • 1 of 3 land, sea, space and sun grant universities in the U.S. • 2 campuses, 11 colleges, 12 experiment stations, and Extension programs in all 36 counties • 7 https://hr.oregonstate.edu/work-life/diversity-and-cultural-resources that offer education, celebration and belonging for everyone • 100+ undergraduate degree programs, 80+ graduate degrees plus hundreds of minor options and certificates • 35k+ students including more than 2.3k international students and 10k students of color • 217k+ alumni worldwide • For more interesting facts about OSU visit: https://oregonstate.edu/about Locations: Oregon State has a statewide presence with campuses in Corvallis and Bend, the OSU Portland Center and the Hatfield Marine Science Center on the Pacific Coast in Newport. Oregon State's beautiful, historic and state-of-the-art main campus is located in one of America's best college towns. Corvallis is located close to the Pacific Ocean, the Cascade mountains and Oregon wine country. Nestled in the heart of the Willamette Valley, this beautiful city offers miles of mountain biking and hiking trails, a river perfect for boating or kayaking and an eclectic downtown featuring local cuisine, popular events and performances. Total Rewards Package: Oregon State University offers a https://hr.oregonstate.edu/benefits/prospective-employee with benefits eligible positions that is designed to meet the needs of employees and their families including: • Medical, Dental, Vision and Basic Life. OSU pays 95% of premiums for you and your eligible dependents. • Free confidential mental health and emotional support services, and counseling resources. • Retirement savings paid by the university. • A generous paid leave package, including holidays, vacation and sick leave. • Tuition reduction benefits for you or your qualifying dependents at OSU or the additional six Oregon Public Universities. • Robust Work Life programs including Dual Career assistance resources, flexible work arrangements, a Family Resource Center, Affinity Groups and an Employee Assistance Program. • Optional lifestyle benefits such as pet, accident, and critical illness insurance, giving you peace of mind and the support you need to thrive in all aspects of your life. Oregon State University is deeply committed to the principles of a Health Promoting University. This commitment drives a collaborative approach across OSU's safety and well-being programs, reducing silos and coordinating efforts to enhance employee safety and well-being. By prioritizing resources that support the health of both employees and students, OSU fosters a culture of care and a healthier campus environment where everyone can thrive. https://bestplace4workingparents.com/policies/ Future and current OSU employees can use the https://hr.oregonstate.edu/benefits/new-employees/benefits-calculator to learn more about the full value of the benefits provided at OSU. Key Responsibilities 100% Instruction • Develop and facilitate non-credit courses for the Professional Development for Educators (PDE) unit• Participate in necessary training and meetings to develop, maintain, and teach appropriate technologies in OSU's learning management system (Canvas).• Experience teaching, training, or facilitating learning or developing curriculum in the course content area.• Courses are expected to promote experiential learning and success of students from varied backgrounds What You Will Need • Bachelor's degree in Education or a closely related field.• Demonstrated ability to design, teach and assess courses that support inclusive learning principles and promote equitable teaching practices, to the benefit of all learners. What We Would Like You to Have • Master's degree in Education or a closely related field.• Experience developing and/or delivering online courses.• One year of experience working as an educator.• Advanced certifications related to techniques and standards of online learning. Working Conditions / Work Schedule Office space is provided in Furman Hall at OSU's Corvallis campus. Regular meetings are required in person or via video conferencing with the manager of PDE. Special Instructions to Applicants Applications will be considered throughout the Spring and Fall 2026 academic year. When applying you will be required to attach the following electronic documents: 1) A resume; and 2) A cover letter indicating how your qualifications and experience have prepared you for this position. You will also be required to submit the names of at least three professional references, their e-mail addresses and telephone numbers as part of the application process. Finalists will be required to provide proof of their degree at the time of offer. Starting salary within the salary range will be commensurate with skills, education, and experience. For additional information please contact:Thomas Fieldthomas.field@oregonstate.edu We are an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability, protected veteran, and other protected status. jobs.description: Employer: Concord University Expires: 10/01/2026 The Department of Business at Concord University invites applications for a tenure-track position in finance at the Assistant/Associate Professor level, effective August 2026. Concord University prides itself on a 150-year tradition of preparing students to enter the workforce or continue their education through graduate studies. We are seeking highly qualified individuals to join our faculty, who can apply their education and work experience to instruction that will enrich our students, further Concord’s commitment to programs of excellence, and reinforce CU’s mission to serve the region. This is a full-time, 9-month tenure-track faculty position that supports the departments’ two degree programs. The Department of Business offers an undergraduate degree program with concentrations in Accounting, Finance, Hospitality Management, Management, Marketing, and Sport Management. The Department also offers a 30-hour MBA program, as well as a Graduate Certificate in Human Resource Management. Faculty members assume an active and collegial role in the planning and governance of the Department’s activities and expectations. Primary responsibilities include: Teaching a variety of undergraduate finance and related business courses (e.g. corporate finance, investments, personal finance, quantitative courses), along with a graduate class in finance with a 4/4 teaching load.Advising and mentoring students, participating in curriculum review and development, assessing and reporting of student learning, and reporting activities for program and university accreditation.Conducting scholarly research and being involved in the professional academic community..Participating in service activities, which include serving on university and departmental committees, as well as service to the broader University community.EducationPh.D. in finance or related area or a DBA with a finance emphasis preferably from a regionally accredited institution. Individuals with a solid research background who are ABD at the final stage of completion of the dissertation may be considered.MBA business or other related master’s degree with substantial profession experience, may be considered for a non-tenure track position.Required SkillsDemonstrate teaching competency and have a strong commitment to, and understanding of, the role of undergraduate and graduate business education.Demonstrate evidence of excellent oral and written English communication skillsProvide evidence of interest in programmatic research and/or a prior record of publishing as we require and support faculty research productivityUnderstand the development of new course offerings in their disciple to support the department’s undergraduate and graduate programs.

jobs.title: Full Time Clinician at DBT Of South Jersey
jobs.description: Employer: DBT Of South Jersey Expires: 10/01/2026 Full Time Clinician, DBT of South JerseyDBT of South Jersey is a counseling and wellness center that provides group, individual counseling services and holistic workshops to support healing. We support children, teens and adults and help them build the life they want through counseling practices that work. We specialize in helping clients gain control over intense emotions, empower them to work through past traumas and develop skills to change their lives.Join the DBT of South Jersey team and be a part of a supportive and collaborative environment that is rooting for the success of both you and those you serve.Why Join DBT of South Jersey:Commitment to Excellence: Be part of the only practice with Linehan Board Certified DBT therapists in South Jersey providing comprehensive care while doing life changing work.Innovative Approach: Embrace a skills-based methodology and holistic approach, including trauma-informed yoga, meditation workshops, and more, reflecting our commitment to whole person healing.Supportive Environment: Work with a team who is dedicated to your success and wellbeing as a therapist.Competency + Expectations:The perfect match for this position is aligned with our core values in their beliefs and actions:Never Stop Learning - We are looking for someone that LOVES to learn. Learning DBT is like learning a new language, and takes time to master. Someone that feels tired or overwhelmed at the thought of learning more would not be a good match.Safe Spaces - Our team works hard to create safe spaces for all humans in order to create the best conditions for healing. Someone that has biases preventing them from doing anti-racism and LGBTQ+ affirming work, for example, would not do well in our practice.Human To Human Connection - We are a feedback driven culture and seek someone who embraces growth, contributes as a supportive team member, and takes accountability. Those who view feedback only as criticism and struggle with accountability won't align well with our team.We operate as a team and are looking for individuals who are seeking out an environment that is supportive and encouraging.Position Details + Hours:Overall, we want you to show up as yourself and no one else. We want to celebrate you as you are. If you are an authentic and genuine human, you will fit in well with our team, which is one of the most important requirements. Otherwise, we also need someone who:Is licensed in New Jersey (LAC/LPC, LSW/LCSW).Isn't afraid to help clients suffering from emotion dysregulation and risk behaviors.Provides counseling services, treatment planning, associated paperwork and case management to an average of 23 clients per week in individual and group sessions.Is willing to work evenings minimally during the first year of employment (see hours below) while building a caseload (working evenings is not required outside of being able to build your caseload).Is excited to offer the real deal DBT, meaning all four modes of comprehensive treatment, including phone coaching and skills group.Strong consideration to those who work with children, adolescents, couples or families, as well as those who have specialized training outside of DBT (Eating Disorders, Substance Use, Somatic Practices, etc.). Also, you do NOT need any previous training in DBT to work with us.Hours:Our goal is to help you move into your dream schedule, and that takes time. We will help coach you on building your caseload to one that is ideal work with the ideal clients at the ideal time for you. It does take time, especially if you are starting from scratch.Here is what we have found is the most effective schedule to get started:2pm-9pm 4 days/week required during caseload building periodCan swap 2-9pm shift for an earlier Friday or Saturday shiftBegin with part time hours to build your caseload to an average of 23 direct client hours per week.Note - Scheduling is flexible and self managed when you have a full caseload, and these hours are not set in stone.DBT consultation team meeting every Tuesday from 11am-12:30pm.DBT telephone coaching for comprehensive clients during weekdays and a shared team rotation for nights + weekends.Measures of Success:To excel in this position, we expect the following measures of success:Maintain a minimum of 23 direct client hours each week.Complete 100% of progress notes and required documentation by Monday at 9am for the previous week.Maintain a client turnover rate of less than 5% on average.Two adherent DBT session tapes within 6 months of hire.Employee Perks + Benefits:Earn competitive wages in a private practice setting but with the benefits of an employee. This means your employer pays into your taxes on your behalf and takes care of virtually everything you need on the business side.LAC/LSW compensation ranges 40$-52$ per clinical hour on averageLPC/LCSW compensation is 60$ per clinical hour on averageWork full time for a job that requires 23 direct clinical hours in your 32 hour work week! Want to make more? You get to decide if you want to take more clients, as opposed to being locked into a salary regardless of how much more work you do.Health Insurance! Medical, dental and vision plans for insurance (We cover 50% of our full time employee plans and have Horizon for our medical plan).Simple IRA with a 2% match for retirement. Eligible from day one.Paid time off with the ability to flex time as you manage your own schedule. Additional paid time off includes: parental leave, compassionate bereavement leave and even a paid hour each November to vote all at a non-clinical rate.Scheduling flexibility (you choose a 4 or 5 day work week - as long as you meet your session requirements, schedule as you wish!) Also, some of your work can be done virtually.Ease into your full time schedule by building your caseload to 23 within a 3 month time frame.Team self care and connection events.Supportive team environment that covers one another when out and shares phone coaching responsibilities.Clinical Training + Supervision:Additional training opportunities and consultation for non DBT topics such as Exposure Response Prevention, Yoga for Trauma, working with children and teens, providing neurodivergent affirming care, and more (we don't JUST do DBT)!LACs and LSWs will have weekly clinical supervision. We offer supervision monthly for fully licensed staff, despite many practices only offering group supervision at this level.We will train you in Dialectical Behavior Therapy immediately and give you all of the tools you need to become a DBT badass!Access to a DBT learning community at no cost to you. This membership comes with monthly consult time (in addition to what you already receive) and NBCC CE's.You will get the highest level of training to ensure you are eligible to become Linehan Board Certified therapist (do you know there are only 14 in NJ and our team has 4 of them right here?!)DBT certification reimbursement of $1,000Supervision opportunities to work a different part of your brain, and get the chance to earn extra income through working with interns.

You can be a part of our vision to be a leader in the integration of physical, mental and social health to make a real difference in the lives of others!We are currently seeking a Therapist to join our team in Children's Program, located in Wayne County, Indiana.About the RoleAs a Therapist, you'll play a vital role for the provision of clinical services to individuals in their respective areas, primarily children, adults and/or families with mental health issues and/or dual diagnosis, or individuals with substance use/dependence issues in both the outpatient and residential setting.Key ResponsibilitiesConduct comprehensive clinical assessments, mental status exams, and diagnosesDevelop and implement individualized treatment plans in collaboration with patientsProvide individual, family, couples, and group counseling servicesDeliver therapeutic services aligned with treatment plansCollaborate with multidisciplinary teams, courts, schools, and community agencies to coordinate careCommunicate effectively with patients, staff, and external partners both verbally and in writingMaintain accurate, timely, and compliant clinical and administrative documentationAdhere to organizational policies, ethical standards, and state and federal regulationsWhat We're Looking ForWe're seeking compassionate, motivated individuals who are passionate about whole-person care and thrive in a collaborative, team-based environment. Experience in behavioral health or social services is a plus.Master's Degree in Social Work, Psychology, Mental Health Counseling, or Marital & Family Therapy, or related Behavioral Science field of study requiredCurrent non-probationary temporary license from state of Indiana in one of the following: LSW, LMHC-A, LMFT-A, LCAC-A required at minimumValid driver's license, a driving record meeting Meridian's driving policy, reliable transportation, and proof of auto insurance requiredWhy Build Your Career at Meridian?At Meridian Health Services, we offer more than a job—we offer a career with purpose, growth, and support. Those who are MD's (US citizenship required), Licensed Clinical Social Workers, Licensed Marriage & Family Therapists and Nurse Practitioners are eligible to apply for loan forgiveness if they work in one of the following qualifying Meridian Health Services' locations.

jobs.description: Employer: Thompson Counseling Services LCSW, PLLC Expires: 10/01/2026 Thompson Counseling ServicesThompson Counseling Services is a therapist-owned group practice in New Paltz, NY, serving children, adolescents, and adults throughout the Hudson Valley. Our mission is to connect community members of all ages with compassionate, skilled therapists who provide treatment that is accessible and sustainable, helping people get the direction and support they need to make the changes they want.We accept all major insurances, including Medicare and Medicaid, because we believe quality mental health care shouldn't be out of reach. Our reputation has been built almost entirely on word of mouth, something we don't take lightly. From the first phone call to the last session, we hold ourselves to a high standard at every touchpoint.We were founded by a clinician, and our values reflect that: excellence in care, integrity, accessibility, and collaboration. We know what therapists need to do their best work, and we've built the infrastructure to support it.The RoleWe're seeking a skilled, dedicated therapist to join our clinical team. This position is based at our New Paltz office, where the majority of sessions are conducted in person. Work with children and adolescents is in person, as we've found that younger clients thrive with the consistency and connection that face-to-face therapy provides. Most of our clients across all ages are currently requesting in-person sessions, so the caseload will be predominantly in person, with some room for hybrid work where it is clinically appropriate.While we are specifically looking for a therapist whose primary focus and passion is working with children and teens, we recognize that a mixed caseload can make for a healthier and more sustainable practice. Clinicians who also enjoy working with young adults and adults will find that balance is naturally supported here.You'll join a practice with an active waiting list, meaning you can focus on clinical work from day one rather than spending months building a caseload.What You'll DoProvide individual in-person therapy clients in an outpatient settingCollaborate with parents and families as part of the therapeutic processMaintain timely, thorough clinical documentationParticipate in supervision and peer consultationUphold the ethical and professional standards that define our practiceWhat Sets Us ApartYou'll have clients from day one. We maintain an active waiting list so you're never starting from scratch.This practice is therapist-owned, which means leadership understands the work because they're doing it too.Strong systems are in place for billing, credentialing, marketing, and office operations so you can focus entirely on care.Weekly individual supervision is provided for limited permit holders (LMSW and MHC-LP), and all clinicians participate in peer supervision and monthly team meetings.Every new clinician goes through an organized onboarding process so you feel supported and set up for success from the start.Scheduling is flexible and built around your availability, including afternoon and evening hours.Full-time staff receive competitive W2 compensation and a full benefits package.All staff are W2, covered under company liability insurance policyYou're a Great Fit If You...Have experience in an outpatient therapeutic setting, diagnosing, creating treatment goals with your clients and meeting on a weekly or biweekly basis to accomplish goals.Are comfortable with and enthusiastic about in-person clinical workAre collaborative, clinically thoughtful, and hold yourself to high documentation standardsWant to grow within a stable, values-driven practice that has earned its reputation through excellent careAre looking for a long-term professional homeRequirementsMaster's degree in Social Work or Mental Health CounselingActive NYS license or permit: LCSW, LMHC, LMSW, or MHC-LP considered on reviewExperience working with children and/or adolescents in an outpatient setting strongly preferredFull-time availability preferredMixed schedule of afternoon and evening availability requiredCommitment to in-person work at our New Paltz officeCompensation & GrowthW2, hourly position paying $35 to $55 per clinical session, commensurate with experience and licensureFull-time position with benefits eligible after a 90-day probationary periodFor clinicians who are looking beyond the clinical hour, TCS offers a career ladder for those interested in growing into supervisory roles and becoming an integral part of the continued growth of our practice. We are building something meaningful here, and we want team members who want to grow with us.How to ApplyPlease send the following directly to our clinical manager, ashley@thompsoncounselingservices.org ResumeCurrent licensure statusBrief cover letter describing your relatable experienceQualified candidates will be contacted for a conversation.BenefitsDental insuranceFlexible scheduleHealth insuranceHealth savings accountPaid time offRetirement planVision insuranceThompson Counseling Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Mental Health Therapist at Transformations Care Network
jobs.description: Employer: Transformations Care Network Expires: 10/01/2026 Join us at Columbia Mental Health, a member of Transformations Care Network (TCN), as we embark on an exciting journey to empower Mental Health Therapists like you to make a difference in the field of behavioral health. We are committed to improving access to mental health care in our communities which means we are committed to being a great place to be a therapist. As a Therapist on our team, you will experience an environment where both you and your clients can thrive. Emerging, early career therapists appreciate a collaborative environment, where they are supported by a clinical team that prioritizes growth and development as they work to gain licensure. Our clinics provide a supportive space to practice therapeutic interventions and develop skills that impact our diverse local community. Licensed Therapists appreciate the ability to practice in a sustainable and personalized way, with the support of a clinical and administrative team. Leadership and supervision opportunities allow our Therapists to build a career that works for them while guiding the next generation of mental health providers. Key Responsibilities Conduct culturally sensitive, strength-based assessments for new clients and families, creating a welcoming and understanding environment for diverse backgrounds. Provide tailored outpatient individual and family therapy based on the unique needs and circumstances of each client, fostering a path to healing and resilience. Develop comprehensive crisis plans, safety plans, relapse prevention plans, and wellness plans, supporting the maintenance of stable functioning and empowering clients in their mental health journey. Actively participate in case consultations, agency meetings, and discharge planning, contributing your expertise to enhance client care. Ensure timely completion of billing, documentation, individualized treatment plans, and insurance authorization forms, upholding the highest standards of professional responsibility. Engage in collaborative care with our team of psychiatrists, nurse practitioners, dietitians, administrative staff, and fellow therapists, to provide a holistic approach to mental health care. Qualifications Possess a Master’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, Marriage and Family Counseling, or a related field. If required, provisional license per state regulation. Educational background that leads to or has resulted in professional licensing. Passionate about mental health and committed to providing high-quality care. Dedicated to ongoing professional development in mental health including free supervision and continuing education. Eager to collaborate with a multidisciplinary team to enhance client care. Strong commitment to ethical practice and maintaining confidentiality. Excellent communication skills and ability to build rapport with clients and families. Ability to manage time effectively and complete documentation and administrative tasks efficiently. Explore the Advantages of Joining Our Team: Enjoy competitive compensation and a wide range of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, low-cost virtual care, dependent and domestic partner coverage, 401K, and more, designed to support your well-being and financial security. Immerse yourself in a community united by a deep commitment to enhance mental health and revolutionize the care that clients receive. Embrace a journey of growth and development through continuous learning, guided by seasoned professionals, fostering your career growth in a nurturing environment. Play a pivotal role in reshaping how mental health care is perceived and delivered in your local community as well as on a national scale, with your efforts directly improving client lives. Deliver mental health care in a sustainable way, with the support and tools you need to thrive. Thrive in an environment that celebrates collaborative success, driven by effective communication, support, and unity. Receive comprehensive onboarding and ongoing educational resources, tailored to cultivate your talents, and assure your triumph in your role. Columbia Mental Health is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The base compensation range for this role is $47 – $55 per billable unit. Actual compensation may vary based on licensure, experience, market-driven enhancements, and incentive opportunities available for this role. These ranges represent our current standard compensation practices and may be adjusted over time to remain competitive and aligned with organizational needs.

jobs.title: CIC Registered Nurse at High Plains Mental Health Center
jobs.description: Employer: High Plains Mental Health Center Expires: 10/01/2026 Now Hiring: Mental Health RN – Starting at $35-46 per hour! APPLICATION DEADLINE: Tuesday, September 22nd, 2026 at 7:00am CDT. Position: CIC Registered Nurse (RN) (PRN)Location: Hays, Kansas | Crisis Intervention CenterPay: Starting at $35-46 per hour [based on experience] | Shift differentials available- earn $1-3 more per hour) | $500 SIGN-ON BONUSJob Type: PRN (as-needed) | In-person | [full-time hours also available]Schedule: Working up to 28 hrs/wk on a PRN basis | Looking for night / overnight coverage WHY YOU SHOULD APPLY:Be a part of history. High Plains Mental Health Center is proud to have launched one of Kansas’s first Crisis Intervention Centers (CIC) — and we want YOU to be part of this groundbreaking journey. This center is already playing a vital role in transforming mental health care across northwest Kansas by easing the burden on local hospitals and law enforcement, shortening inpatient waitlists, and providing critical mental health services close to home for those in need.As a 24/7 inpatient facility, the CIC offers multiple shifts and a variety of career opportunities. Now is the time to raise your hand and secure your spot! For more information about the Crisis Intervention Center (CIC), please visit: [HPMHC CIC].If you’re ready for a rewarding opportunity, and want to be supported by an organization that stands by its mission of being “Here for You,” this is your chance. APPLY TODAY! WHAT YOU’LL DO:As an RN at the CIC, you’ll provide essential nursing care, crisis stabilization, and medication management to individuals in acute mental health distress, including those with co-occurring substance use disorders. You’ll be part of a multidisciplinary team supporting patient stabilization, safety, and recovery. Key responsibilities include:· Conducting nursing assessments and monitoring patient status throughout their stay.· Administering medications and monitoring effects under psychiatric supervision.· Using crisis intervention and de-escalation techniques to ensure a safe environment.· Supporting suicide prevention, seclusion/restraint protocols, and trauma-informed practices.· Documenting all clinical activity accurately and timely.· Educating patients and families on mental health care and recovery strategies.· Collaborating closely with physicians, APRNs, and the broader treatment team, helping to ensure continuity of care.· Ensuring regulatory compliance and upholding patient dignity in every interaction. WHY JOIN US?At High Plains Mental Health Center, we’re here for you — not only for the individuals and communities we serve, but for every member of our team. Our mission drives everything we do, and that includes supporting our employees with the same compassion, dedication, and care we offer our clients.When you join us, you become part of a purpose-driven organization where your work has a real impact. You’ll provide critical mental health services to those who need them most, while being part of a team that values your expertise, supports your well-being, and invests in your professional growth through continuous learning and career advancement opportunities. QUALIFICATIONS:· Must be 21+ years old with current Kansas RN licensure (ADN or BSN).· Preferred, but not required: one year of psychiatric nursing, crisis intervention, emergency care, or inpatient experience.· Strong knowledge of behavioral health crisis care, psychiatric medications, and trauma-informed care.· Must maintain CPR and First Aid certification (provided by our Center).· Must pass all required background checks (KBI, KDADS).· Physically capable of working in high-pressure situations and responding to emergencies.· Must comply with TB testing and health screening protocols.· Muss pass pre-employment drug screening.· Must maintain a valid driver’s license; [MVR will be checked]. No substance-related driving offenses in the past 5 years. SUBMIT YOUR APPLICATION:If you’re ready to take the next step in your career and make a difference in the future of mental health services, we want to hear from you! APPLY TODAY using this link: [HPMHC CAREERS!]If you have any questions or need help with documentation, please feel free to contact CAREERS@HPMH.COM. High Plains Mental Health Center – We’re Here For You!

jobs.description: Employer: High Plains Mental Health Center Expires: 10/01/2026 Outpatient Therapist Needed – Apply Now to Join a Supportive Team APPLICATION DEADLINE: Wednesday, September 23rd, 2026 at 7:00am CDT. Location: Phillipsburg, Kansas | High Plains Mental Health CenterPay: from $64,218 salary | Incentive Pay | $7,500-9,000 SIGN-ON BONUSJob Type: Full-Time | In-PersonSchedule: Monday – Friday 8am-5pm (+ >3 hours outside normal business hours per week | 40 hours / week total) Why You Should Apply:As an Outpatient Therapist at High Plains Mental Health Center, you’ll provide individual, family, and group therapy to clients with a wide range of mental health needs. You’ll receive regular clinical supervision, case consultation, and support from experienced supervisors who are actively involved in your development. APPLY TODAY! jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Program Facilitator at Play Like a Girl!®
jobs.description: Employer: Play Like a Girl!® Expires: 10/01/2026 Paid, part-time, seasonal | $25 per hourLocations: Boston, Dallas, Nashville, and New OrleansYou’re the person who brings the energy, remembers names, and notices the girl who hasn’t found her moment yet. Bring that gift to Play Like a Girl. You’ll lead engaging activities, help girls connect with mentors, and capture the moments that show their curiosity, confidence, and growth. About Play Like a GirlPlay Like a Girl is a national nonprofit dedicated to leveling the playing field for girls in sports and STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics). For over 20 years, we’ve helped girls build confidence, leadership, and skills for competitive careers in male-dominated fields through mentorship, teamwork, and education. Headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, we operate remotely with a collaborative, innovative, and high-performing team committed to expanding opportunities for girls and young women nationwide. The OpportunityUsing our ready-to-use curriculum, you’ll lead group activities, support mentoring conversations, and help middle school girls set goals and recognize their progress. You’ll also capture approved photos, video clips, and stories for our communications.This role is especially well suited to college juniors and seniors interested in education, youth development, communications, sports, STEM, social work, psychology, or nonprofit leadership. All majors are welcome. Campus leadership, athletics, volunteering, caregiving, and paid work count as relevant experience. Schedule and LocationProgram: Twelve one-hour school sessions, with six in the fall and six in the spring.Hours: Approximately 5–7 paid hours per active program week at one site, including preparation, travel, setup, facilitation, documentation, storytelling, and approved outreach.Availability: Assigned weekday sessions within the noon–6 p.m. local-time window, plus a required virtual team meeting every Monday, 11 a.m.–12:30 p.m. Central Time.Location: Live within 30 miles of your selected city and have reliable transportation to your assigned site. Approved planning, writing, and team collaboration may be completed remotely.Your assignment and schedule will be confirmed before you accept an offer. Additional school assignments and hours will be discussed separately. What You’ll DoLead welcoming, interactive sessions. Prepare activities, explain instructions clearly, keep groups engaged, and make room for different personalities and participation styles.Support mentoring and learning. Brief mentors, guide balanced conversations, and help girls explore interests, practice skills, and track goals.Keep programs organized. Coordinate with school contacts, support reminders and forms, and maintain attendance and session records.Capture and tell meaningful stories. With verified permission and appropriate supervision coverage, collect photos, clips, voluntary quotes, and observations. Organize materials and develop stories for blogs, email, social media, and video, following organizational approval procedures.Build local connections. Share approved opportunities with relevant community networks.Learn and communicate. Participate in training and coaching, apply feedback, and promptly raise concerns or support needs.What You’ll BringExperience leading, coaching, teaching, mentoring, or caring for a group.Warmth, positive energy, clear communication, and sound judgment.The ability to adjust an activity, include quieter participants, and set kind, consistent boundaries.Reliable attendance, preparation, organization, and follow-through.Clear writing and basic photo or video skills.Willingness to complete required background screening and youth-safety training before working with participants. Camp counseling, orientation leadership, resident advising, tutoring, cheerleading, coaching, and student organizations are all relevant. Experience with middle school students, Canva, CapCut, or campus communications is helpful but not required. You don’t need a STEM degree or professional equipment. Team and SupportYou’ll report to the Program Coordinator and work with school partners, mentors, volunteers, and fellow facilitators. You’ll receive curriculum, materials, training, regular coaching, and support with program challenges. Success MeasuresWe’ll evaluate your success through:Session readiness: Prepared materials, clear instructions, and smooth transitions.Inclusive engagement: Activities that welcome different participation styles and help girls feel included.Mentor preparation: Mentors who understand their roles and contribute to productive group conversations.Timely documentation: Accurate attendance and session notes submitted within 24 hours.Responsible storytelling: Organized, permission-checked content submitted within 48 hours when consent and safe coverage allow, plus accurate story drafts completed by agreed deadlines.Communication and follow-through: Prompt reporting of concerns and completion of assigned program and outreach tasks.Growth: Observable improvement through coaching and participant feedback. Pay and PerksYou’ll earn $25 per hour for all authorized work, including training, preparation, meetings, program delivery, documentation, storytelling, and outreach.You’ll gain practical leadership and communications experience, regular coaching, connections with educators and professionals, and opportunities to build an approved portfolio of your work. How to Apply and What Happens NextOne application covers all five cities. Select your preferred city and provide your availability.Complete Stage One. After applying, you’ll receive an email with full instructions: a scenario for a welcome video of up to 90 seconds and a fictional participant story to turn into a 250–350-word blog post and a social caption of up to 75 words.Email your submissions. Send them to jobs@iplaylikeagirl.org with the subject Stage One Submission | Program Facilitator | [Your Full Name]. Attach your work or provide viewable links.Attend a virtual interview. Selected applicants will be invited to a 20-minute conversation about their experience, availability, and approach to working with girls.Demonstrate your facilitation skills. Finalists will complete a virtual simulation using a Play Like a Girl activity shared in advance. Hiring TimelineApplications: Priority consideration by September 18, 2026; final deadline September 21.Interviews and finalist activities: Scheduled virtually on a rolling basis.Offers: Extended by September 25.Virtual onboarding: September 28–October 1, with screening and pre-work completed by October 2.In-person training and parent orientation: An assigned date in your city between October 5 and October 12, confirmed before you accept an offer.Program start: October 13 or later, according to your school’s schedule.Ready to help girls feel welcome, try something new, and see what they’re capable of? We’d love to hear from you.Equal OpportunityPlay Like a Girl is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We encourage applications from rural residents, people of color, women, LGBTQ+ individuals, and others from historically marginalized groups.

jobs.title: Mental Health Therapist at Transformations Care Network
jobs.description: Employer: Transformations Care Network Expires: 10/01/2026 oin us at Columbia Mental Health, a member of Transformations Care Network (TCN), as we embark on an exciting journey to empower Mental Health Therapists like you to make a difference in the field of behavioral health. We are committed to improving access to mental health care in our communities which means we are committed to being a great place to be a therapist. As a Therapist on our team, you will experience an environment where both you and your clients can thrive. Emerging, early career therapists appreciate a collaborative environment, where they are supported by a clinical team that prioritizes growth and development as they work to gain licensure. Our clinics provide a supportive space to practice therapeutic interventions and develop skills that impact our diverse local community. Licensed Therapists appreciate the ability to practice in a sustainable and personalized way, with the support of a clinical and administrative team. Leadership and supervision opportunities allow our Therapists to build a career that works for them while guiding the next generation of mental health providers. Key Responsibilities Conduct culturally sensitive, strength-based assessments for new clients and families, creating a welcoming and understanding environment for diverse backgrounds. Provide tailored outpatient individual and family therapy based on the unique needs and circumstances of each client, fostering a path to healing and resilience. Develop comprehensive crisis plans, safety plans, relapse prevention plans, and wellness plans, supporting the maintenance of stable functioning and empowering clients in their mental health journey. Actively participate in case consultations, agency meetings, and discharge planning, contributing your expertise to enhance client care. Ensure timely completion of billing, documentation, individualized treatment plans, and insurance authorization forms, upholding the highest standards of professional responsibility. Engage in collaborative care with our team of psychiatrists, nurse practitioners, dietitians, administrative staff, and fellow therapists, to provide a holistic approach to mental health care. Qualifications Possess a Master’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, Marriage and Family Counseling, or a related field. If required, provisional license per state regulation. Educational background that leads to or has resulted in professional licensing. Passionate about mental health and committed to providing high-quality care. Dedicated to ongoing professional development in mental health including free supervision and continuing education. Eager to collaborate with a multidisciplinary team to enhance client care. Strong commitment to ethical practice and maintaining confidentiality. Excellent communication skills and ability to build rapport with clients and families. Ability to manage time effectively and complete documentation and administrative tasks efficiently. Explore the Advantages of Joining Our Team: Enjoy competitive compensation and a wide range of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, low-cost virtual care, dependent and domestic partner coverage, 401K, and more, designed to support your well-being and financial security. Immerse yourself in a community united by a deep commitment to enhance mental health and revolutionize the care that clients receive. Embrace a journey of growth and development through continuous learning, guided by seasoned professionals, fostering your career growth in a nurturing environment. Play a pivotal role in reshaping how mental health care is perceived and delivered in your local community as well as on a national scale, with your efforts directly improving client lives. Deliver mental health care in a sustainable way, with the support and tools you need to thrive. Thrive in an environment that celebrates collaborative success, driven by effective communication, support, and unity. Receive comprehensive onboarding and ongoing educational resources, tailored to cultivate your talents, and assure your triumph in your role. Columbia Mental Health is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The base compensation range for this role is $47 – $55 per billable unit. Actual compensation may vary based on licensure, experience, market-driven enhancements, and incentive opportunities available for this role. These ranges represent our current standard compensation practices and may be adjusted over time to remain competitive and aligned with organizational needs. Transformations Care Network is an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace.
